description: Azure Digital Twins is Microsoft's platform as a service for building twin graphs from digital models of whole environments such as buildings, factories, farms, energy networks, railways, stadiums and cities. Users define the people, places and things of an environment as custom twin types, called models, in the JSON-like Digital Twins Definition Language (DTDL), describing their state properties, components and relationships; a building management solution might define Building, Floor and Elevator types, and ready-made DTDL industry ontologies can be used as a starting point. The service connects to IoT Hub device twins to send and receive live data, routes events for business logic and data processing, lets users query the live twin graph and historised data, and supports connected 3D visualisation and integration with other Azure analytics and AI services. Microsoft notes that it is distinct from the digital twin builder preview in Fabric and from IoT Hub device twins. Coverage: generic. Access: an Azure subscription, with a pricing calculator by region and a free Azure trial. Licence: commercial cloud service. Caveats: solutions must be built on the service, and prices vary by agreement, region and currency. Simulation uses: live building and campus twin graphs for operations, space use and energy analytics. Related records: RealEstateCore, Brick Schema, Bentley iTwin and Autodesk Tandem.
